title: Unified asset intake/review/organize pipeline (images + audio)
summary: artwork/in-tray/ and audio/in-tray/ both follow the same shape: drop raw files in, AI examines and describes each one and proposes a purpose, a human reviews/confirms via some kind of backend UI, and only on confirmation does the file get renamed/organized/moved into the real working structure (audio additionally gets compressed to MP3, with the source WAV then discarded).
description:
Two parallel raw-asset intake trees exist on disk: artwork/in-tray/ (confirmed: ~265 files already sorted into rough buckets — scenes 128, character-portraits 66 plus environment/mitflits/aliens/vehicles subfolders, mechs 12, landscapes 4) and audio/in-tray/ (confirmed: ~193 raw WAV files in an 'unorganised' folder, mostly ambience/environment/SFX per the user's own estimate of ~90%, plus one real ElevenLabs-generated test line already sitting in dialogue/control — total audio tree already at 7.2GB).

Workflow for both, as described:
1. Files land in the in-tray unsorted (filenames are often generic/uninformative — e.g. artwork's scenes are literally 'bar_01.png' etc. — so filename alone can't drive organization).
2. Each asset gets examined (visually for images, presumably by listening/transcribing for audio) and a description written — for images specifically, this description becomes context used when writing scenes/dialogue so scene text stays consistent with what the art actually shows.
3. A review backend lets the user listen to/view the asset, check the generated metadata and proposed purpose, correct anything wrong, and hit confirm.
4. Only on confirmation does the asset get moved out of the in-tray into an organized, purpose-assigned location — explicitly to prevent the same piece of art (or sound) accidentally getting used for two different things.
5. For audio specifically: on confirmation, compress the source WAV down to MP3 (space is a real concern — already ~7.2GB from a partial batch) and delete the WAV afterward, since it can always be re-downloaded from the original source if ever needed again.

This revises (not replaces) the asset-pipeline section of design/foundry-module-design.md §3, which assumed asset triage was a purely manual local sort I'd do directly. The review-and-confirm backend with human-in-the-loop approval is new scope beyond what that section currently describes, and should get folded back into that doc once designed further.

**2026-09-17 — the AUDIO half of this pipeline is BUILT** (`tools/audio-pipeline/`, `design/audio-system.md`): intake -> analyse (EBU R128 loudness, silence, real decoded duration) -> propose (kind/category/title/tags, with its reasons recorded) -> process (Ogg Opus, normalised per kind, seamless crossfaded loops for beds) -> verify (every file decodes strictly, hashes match, lands on target) -> upload (checksummed both sides). 398 assets, 8.36 GB of sources -> 785 MB. TWO DELIBERATE DEPARTURES from this entry as written: (1) sources are NEVER moved or deleted -- the WAV originals stay in the in-tray, because a processed file is reproducible and an original is not; (2) the format is Ogg Opus rather than MP3, checked with Ingram (Chrome-only table), which is smaller AND loops without a gap. STILL UNBUILT: the listen-and-confirm review UI. Decisions are hand-edited in `data/audio/review.json` today, and the Sound Desk's audition key covers 'hear it before you decide'. The IMAGE half of this pipeline is untouched by this work.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump. Directory structure independently confirmed on disk the same session.
openSubQuestions: What form the review backend actually takes — a local web tool, something inside the Foundry module, something else entirely?
Exact metadata schema for a cataloged image asset (description, proposed purpose/domains, tags) and audio asset (description, category, proposed use-trigger).
Audio compression specifics: target normalization level, MP3 bitrate/quality.
